title: Fault Category: Process-Level Faults
content:
# Fault Category: Process-Level Faults

A DataNode's process is killed, suspended, or hung. Symptoms range from an immediate connection refusal (process gone) to a full socket-timeout hang (process alive but unresponsive). Affected DataNodes stop serving requests; other replicas continue normally.

title: Fault Category: System-Level Faults
content:
# Fault Category: System-Level Faults

A DataNode's host becomes dead, network-unreachable, or forced read-only. Symptoms include connection refusal, network routing errors, or (for read-only) a pure latency degradation on the write path with no exception at all.

title: Fault Category: Network-Level Faults
content:
# Fault Category: Network-Level Faults

Network conditions between clients/DataNodes are degraded: a specific node disconnected (routing failure), a specific node slowed (latency injection), or the whole cluster's network path uniformly slowed. Distinguish single-node vs. cluster-wide by comparing one DataNode's average against its peers within the same trace.

title: Fault Category: Data-Level Faults
content:
# Fault Category: Data-Level Faults

A block's data or metadata is corrupted, truncated, or lost. Metadata corruption fails before any transfer (implausible checksum values); data corruption fails mid-transfer (checksum mismatch on real data); truncation/loss fails with a length mismatch or an explicit 'not valid' block state.

title: Fault Category: Real Hadoop Bug Reproductions
content:
# Fault Category: Real Hadoop Bug Reproductions

Genuine (not synthetically injected) Hadoop defects reproduced under specific workload conditions, most often surfacing as extreme, pathological latency in a particular operation rather than a clean single-cause symptom.

title: Fault Category: Multi-Fault Combination (AnarchyApe)
content:
# Fault Category: Multi-Fault Combination (AnarchyApe)

Several fault conditions injected simultaneously. Symptoms can still localize to a single component, but more than one condition may be present — don't stop investigating after the first plausible cause.
